title: Market origination order — side first, then total, then moneyline
description: The mandated order in which this programme originates a game's markets. The side is originated first because it is the anchor quantity: both the total and the moneyline are downstream of the same scoring decomposition, and publishing the side first forces the model to commit to a margin before any dependent market is priced.
columns_rule: Every market we originate publishes three SEPARATE columns: the model's fair line (MODEL OUTPUT, versioned), the market line (SOURCE, third-party flagged — no official NFL price source exists), and the difference (COMPUTED). No cell is ever inferred: where the model has no fitted parameter (totals), the fair and difference cells stay blank and are flagged.

order.inputs: Causal pre-game Elo (K=20, HFA=48, inter-season regression), fixed spread conversion 10.8*log10(p/(1-p))
order.why_first: The margin is the anchor quantity. Total and moneyline both decompose from the same scoring view; originating the side first fixes the model's committed margin before anything dependent is priced.

order.status: BLOCKED — structure published, fair line blank
order.inputs: Stage S2 scoring-rate model (possessions x efficiency). Parameters are deliberately unfitted in this repository.
order.why_second: The total is the second quantity the model must commit to (pace/efficiency view). It is published as a column set so the gap is visible, but the fair value stays BLANK because no parameter has been fitted — filling it would be a fabrication.

order.inputs: The same win probability p that produced the side, converted to American odds (p clipped to [0.02, 0.98]); differences published in implied-probability percentage points vs the market's raw implied probability (vig included).
order.why_third: The moneyline is a restatement of the side's win probability in price form; originating it last prevents it from leaking information back into the margin.

origination_policy: Every release re-originates in this order: side, total, moneyline.
A model number is never published without its model version and basis (pre-game causal vs snapshot).
A market number is never published without its provenance label (third-party flagged until a licensed/official price feed lands behind the price-snapshot store).
The difference column is computed, never typed: fair minus market, with the sign convention stated on the page.
Player props and parlays are NOT originated in v1 (prop settlement definitions and joint pricing are blocked — see questions.html).
